definition: Commit time of one gateway epoch = Gateway.commit (unit leaves, Merkle root, CtS thresholds = features + 120-epoch rolling statistics + utility, metadata store with the committed τ column and H(store), C^st, header, Ed25519 signature) of a real epoch of the E5 rev1 run (lp_iot23_34-1_p10000, epoch 400, 238 units, 163 payload) plus N flood units of ONE compromised device; median over reps; single core (P = performance, E = efficiency core via taskpolicy -b), Python prototype, OMP 1 thread. kind zero = random-port SYN scan (one unit per packet: N/30 SYN per second); payload = one-packet TCP units with 16 B payload. history single = the real 119 preceding epochs; sustained = the same flood in every preceding epoch (the rolling statistics span 120 flooded epochs). impl resort = the original RollingDeviceStats (re-sorts the whole window every epoch: the code as reviewed); incremental = the rev1 bit-exact IncrementalRollingStats (O(n_e + n_{e-W})). cap = zero-payload cap of protocol/flood.py (k_dev = 8,192 per device, k_tot = 16,384 per epoch; never binds on any training or test stream), its own cost included in commit_plus_cap; ucap = the policy's utility cap (4,096 scored payload units per device and epoch; never binds on our data).
notes: two rounds ahead (designated round r0+e+2): the build budget grows by one drand period, but a sustained flood also needs commit ≤ T = 30 s per epoch on average (one commit per epoch on the same core); content then waits ≤ 2T + Δ_c + Δ_sel ≈ 63.5 s (E6 buffer ahead2) and the adaptive design of epoch e can only use selections up to e − 2

supported n = largest flood (units per epoch from one device) whose median commit (+ cap) time fits the budget, log-log interpolation between measured points; None = even the smallest measured flood exceeds it

E.note: per-packet pipeline (reader, parser, flow table, gateway, cached H(θ)): it bounds the sustainable packet rate of any flood independently of the commit window (a 10^6-unit/epoch SYN scan is ≈ 33 k packets/s)
